findings.asserts: No test reaches the request-deadline/body-read ordering in web/src/lib/api.ts call(). The Playwright suite (web/e2e/*.spec.ts) contains no page.route / route.fulfill / HAR interception and never stalls a response body; there are no vitest/unit tests for web/src (web/package.json declares only test:e2e/test:visual). The only test that touches the timeout at all is internal/zzprobe/audit7/z08frontendbrowser/bundle_sinks_test.go TestZ08BuiltBundleDoesNotPersistSecretsInWebStorage, which merely asserts the string 'AbortController' exists in the built bundle as a positive control that it is reading api.ts.
findings.gap_note: Nothing proves the AbortController deadline survives `await res.text()` (clearTimeout at api.ts:354 happens before the body read at :369). Harness needed: a Playwright test that page.route-fulfils a response whose headers arrive but whose body never completes (or is delayed past 15s), then asserts the page leaves '正在读取授权请求…' / the session spinner and renders a network_error alert; alternatively a vitest unit test with fake timers and a mocked fetch whose res.text() never resolves, asserting ApiError('network_error') by 15s. Neither a Node unit-test runner nor any route interception exists in the repo.

findings.asserts: The only test that reads web/vite.config.ts is internal/webui/webui_test.go TestBasePathMatchesViteConfig; it regex-extracts `paths.base` and compares it with webui.BasePath, and never invokes the dev-server plugin/middleware or supplies a request target, so the `path === '/'` comparison against req.url (including any query string) is never executed.
findings.gap_note: The dev root redirect (vite.config.ts:27-28) has no coverage at all. Harness needed: extract the plugin's configureServer middleware (or refactor it into an exported function) and call it with mock req/res/next for target '/?error=access_denied', asserting a 302 to /app/?error=access_denied and that next() is not called; or boot a vite dev/connect server in a Node test and GET the URL. web/package.json configures no Node test runner (only Playwright against the built SPA), so a new harness is required.

findings.test_func: a denied login started from the home page still explains itself
findings.asserts: Starts anonymous on /app/, clicks the GitHub provider (which runs SignIn.svelte begin() and builds return_to from page.url.pathname+search), lets the fake IdP deny, then asserts the browser lands on /app/?error=access_denied, that '登录已取消，或未获得授权。' is visible and that no session was created. It pins only the anonymous error-read half of the flow.
findings.gap_note: No test performs a SUCCESSFUL sign-in from a URL that already carries ?error=..., so nothing asserts whether the stale code is forwarded through return_to and re-raised in the signed-in view. Needed: park at /app/?error=access_denied, complete the real GitHub flow, and assert the signed-in account view shows no '登录没有完成'/'身份操作没有完成' alert and that the URL no longer carries error (as it would if the recommendation clears it with history.replaceState).

findings.asserts: Reads web/src/routes/+page.svelte as source text and asserts that every redirectCode the login plane can emit appears as a quoted case label, so a known code always has a friendly sentence. It is a text-presence check, not an execution of authErrorMessage, and it makes no assertion about the unknown-code default branch. web/e2e/login.spec.ts likewise only exercises the known codes access_denied and provider_unavailable.
findings.gap_note: The default branch `登录没有完成（${code}）。` (+page.svelte:82), which echoes an attacker-chosen value into the branded danger Alert, is never exercised with an unrecognised code and has no length cap assertion. Needed: a Playwright test that loads /app/?error=<crafted/long string> and asserts the attacker string is NOT present in the rendered alert (a fixed sentence is shown) and that a huge value cannot be rendered; or a small unit test of authErrorMessage's default branch.

findings.test_func: the account can export its data and then erase itself
findings.asserts: Signs in, clicks '导出我的数据' and awaits Playwright's 'download' event, asserting suggestedFilename() matches /^re0auth-account-usr_/; then walks the two-step erase. It drives exportData() end to end (so data.profile.user_id is read and URL.revokeObjectURL(url) runs at +page.svelte:162-164) but asserts only the filename, never the revocation timing or a malformed envelope.
findings.gap_note: The test cannot see the synchronous revoke because Playwright's download event fires from a.click()/the a.download attribute regardless of whether the blob URL is still readable, and no test returns an envelope without `profile`. Needed: (a) a route-interception test that fulfils /v1/account/export with `{}` or `{"data":{}}` and asserts a recoverable ApiError('malformed_response') message instead of 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'user_id\')', and (b) a unit test spying on URL.createObjectURL/revokeObjectURL ordering (revoke after the download macrotask).

findings.test_func: unlinking an identity can be backed out of
findings.asserts: Clicks '解绑' then '取消', which runs cancelUnlink -> void restoreFocus(`[data-unlink="${id}"]`), and asserts the identity row and both '解绑' buttons are visible again. It never asserts document.activeElement, never uses an id containing a double quote, backslash or ']', and would pass unchanged if the interpolated selector threw a SyntaxError. web/e2e/sources.spec.ts 'a disconnection can be backed out of' exercises the data-disconnect twin the same way; web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts only runs axe on settled pages.
findings.gap_note: No focus assertion and no adversarial identifier. Needed: a browser test that cancels the unlink/disconnect confirmation and asserts the re-created trigger has focus (expect(trigger).toBeFocused()), plus a case where the identity/source id contains a quote or ']' (requires a test-controlled identifier) proving restoreFocus still returns focus instead of producing an unhandled SyntaxError from document.querySelector.

findings.test_func: a source can be connected, used, and disconnected
findings.asserts: Drives /app/sources through connect/disconnect/cascade with one catalogue source and one binding, so the reactive connectable derivation (sources/+page.svelte:89) and resourcesFor() (line 82, used at line 288) execute; but it asserts only card/button visibility and server-side effects, and it never scales available x bindings or measures work per render.
findings.gap_note: The O(available x bindings) rescan cost is unverified. Needed: a benchmark or a browser test with a large injected catalogue/binding set (page.route-fulfil /v1/sources and /v1/bindings with e.g. 1k entries) that pins per-render work - e.g. a unit test of a derived Map/Set with a counting resourcesFor/key, or a timing budget on repeated cancel/confirm clicks. No unit-test harness exists for the Svelte page.

findings.asserts: Mounts httpapi's real middleware chain over a synthetic build, GETs /app/, requires Cache-Control to be exactly 'no-cache', then t.Errorf()s when both ETag and Last-Modified are empty ('no-cache can never become a 304'). It asserts the expected validator, so it is RED while S12-8 is open and turns green when a validator is added. Companion probes: internal/zzprobe/verifyfrontend/verify_frontend_test.go TestVShellCannotBeConditionallyValidatedAtAll (tag audit5) asserts the defective half - no ETag/Last-Modified and no If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since/If-Range request ever yields 304; internal/zzprobe/audit7/z08verify/z08verify_test.go TestZ08VComposedStaticFacts repeats the no-validator assertion against a freshly built binary; internal/webui/webui_test.go TestHandlerServesFilesAndFallsBackToShell asserts the no-cache value itself. All three probes are behind //go:build audit5/audit7, so a default `go test ./...` does not compile them.

No test drives the SPA's retry branch (api.ts:358-361). The Playwright suite never returns 502/503/504 to the app (no route interception exists), and the Go retry tests (httpclient/retry_test.go) cover a different, server-side client, not web/src/lib/api.ts. Nothing observes whether the discarded 5xx Response body is cancelled or drained.
findings.gap_note: Needed: a Playwright test that page.route-fulfils a GET endpoint with 503 (optionally Retry-After), lets the client retry to success, and proves the first response body was released - e.g. by forcing a fresh connection (Connection: close on the 503) and asserting the socket/connection count, or a unit test with a mocked fetch spying on Response.body.cancel()/arrayBuffer(). No test harness for either exists.

findings.asserts: No test feeds a malformed success envelope to the SPA. internal/httpapi/webcontract_test.go TestFrontendProblemCodesMatchCatalogue only parses the ProblemCode union out of api.ts; the /app/admin route has no Playwright spec at all (web/e2e contains no admin spec), and no test loads a page whose GET 200 body lacks `data`/`profile`, so the render-time TypeError and the +error.svelte page.error.message fallback are never reached.
findings.gap_note: Needed: a Playwright test that page.route-fulfils a 200 with a shape missing `data` (e.g. {} for /v1/admin/clients or /v1/grants) and asserts the user sees a fixed recoverable message rather than +error.svelte rendering the raw JS TypeError; if the fix adds envelope validation in call(), add a case per indexed wrapper. Requires a built SPA (present) plus route interception, which the suite currently never uses.

findings.asserts: Serves shell and hashed assets through webui.Handler and asserts body, Cache-Control and CSP, so the Built(), isFile() and ServeFileFS calls on the hot path (webui.go:106/119/133) execute; it makes no claim about how many embedded-FS stats occur or what they cost.
findings.gap_note: Needed: an allocation/bench test over GET /app/_app/immutable/... (e.g. testing.Benchmark with ReportAllocs) or a stat-counting decorator around the fs.FS passed to Handler that asserts one stat + one open per request. Handler currently takes a bare fs.FS, so the harness is to wrap it with a counting fs.FS and assert the count; no such test or benchmark exists in internal/webui.

findings.test_func: signing in from consent returns to the pending request
findings.asserts: Starts anonymous on a real /oauth/authorize consent URL, clicks the provider and asserts the browser returns to /app/consent?id=... signed in - so SignIn.svelte begin() with returnTo constructs and transmits return_to for a start_url that has no fragment. web/e2e/device.spec.ts 'signing in from the device page keeps the user code' exercises the same path for the device page. Neither test asserts anything about URL fragments.
findings.gap_note: No test gives provider.start_url a fragment, so the string-concatenation placement of return_to after '#...' (SignIn.svelte:50-52) is unverified. Needed: a deployment/fake whose provider start_url carries a fragment, then a browser test asserting return_to still reaches the server and the pending consent/device task survives; or a unit test of begin()'s URL construction comparing it with new URL(start_url, origin).searchParams.set('return_to', ...).
